key_insight: Yb-stabilized zirconia coating exhibits an "anomalous solid solution" behavior that raises ZrO2 melting resistance and thermal protection capability without sacrificing high-temperature stability.
engineering_relevance: This suggests a new compositional design route for ultra-high-temperature thermal protection coatings in plasma-sprayed UHTC systems.
method: Atmospheric plasma sprayed ytterbia-stabilized zirconia (YbSZ) coatings.
Evaluated melting-point elevation and ablation resistance under extreme plasma and oxyacetylene heating.
Attributed performance gains to strengthened ionic-covalent mixed bonding and improved oxygen vacancy stability.
evidence_signal: The abstract reports a ZrO2 melting point of about 2850 °C and ultimate plasma/oxyacetylene ablation temperatures of nearly 2780 °C and 3200 °C, respectively.
watch_item: The reported gains are based on a specific YbSZ composition and spray route, so scalability and long-term cyclic durability in service still need validation.
paper_title: "Anomalous Solid Solution" in Ultra-High Melting Point Oxides: A New Strategy for Developing Ultra-High Temperature Thermal Protection Coatings
